summary: Burton Stein was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1966–1988) and SOAS University of London (~1989–1996).

Burton Watson studied at Columbia University (B.A. 1946–1951, PhD ~1950–1956) under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University. Specializing in Sinology and Japanology, he taught at Doshisha, Kyoto, Columbia (Professor, 1961), and Stanford (~1964–1965).

Byambyn Rinchen worked in linguistics, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute (~1924–1927) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1956), and held a post at the National University of Mongolia (~1942).
Byung-gon Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Rissho University (attested 2007). He held posts as professor, dean, and institute director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, C. D. Sebastian earned a PhD from Banaras Hindu University, studying under Ashok Kumar Chatterjee and Abhimanyu Singh, with postdoctoral mentoring by Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa. He taught at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. Pierce Salguero studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (PhD ~2005–2010). Working in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, he held posts at Pennsylvania State University (2010), the University of Pennsylvania (2011–2012), and Asian Medicine (2016).
C. R. Krishnamacharlu worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Madras Christian College (F. A.) and Pachaiyappa's College.

C. R. Lama specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, held a post at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1997), and taught James Low and Andreas Ruft.
C. S. Srinivasachari was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. Scott Littleton worked in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1954–1965) under Jaan Puhvel (~1957–1965).

C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis O. Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as professor at Hartwick College (~2000–2020).
Caixi Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti studied at Presidency College, Kolkata, under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served at the Government Museum Chennai, Indian Museum, Archaeological Survey of India (~1946–1955), and National Museum, New Delhi (attested 1952).

Calvert Watkins studied at Harvard (PhD ~1954–1959), EPHE, and DIAS. A linguist and Indologist, he was a professor at Harvard (1959–2003) and UCLA (2003–2013), and founded the East Coast Indo-European Conference in 1982.

Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Florida State University, and the University of Oxford (Wolfson College), working under Richard F. Nance, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Ulrike Roesler, among others.
Cameron David Warner specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yudru Tsomu and has held posts at Middlebury College, Dickinson College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas and held a postdoctoral fellowship at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti studied at the University of Milan and works in Indology. He has held posts at the University of Cambridge (2011–2014), SOAS University of London, the Bodleian Library (attested 2019), and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Carel Gabriel Cobet was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1832–1836) after Gymnasium Haganum. He held posts at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884, teaching Hendrik Kern and Willem Caland.

Carl A. P. Ruck works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1958–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1965), and held a post at Boston University (~1970).
